label: prf:meson-kaon-pion-hecke-seifert
title: Proof of meson kaon pion hecke seifert
html:
Proof. The algebraic factor arises from the Hecke representation theory of H_3(q_0). On the standard (2,1) irreducible representation, \sigma_1 acts diagonally in the Hoefsmit seminormal basis with eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} (cf. prop:hoefsmit-binding-amplitude). The character of \sigma_1^n for odd n is therefore

  \chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^n)
  = q^n + (-q^{-1})^n
  = q^n - q^{-n}
  = h \cdot [n]_q.

The topological factor uses the Seifert fibration of the torus knot complements. The Seifert Euler number of T(2,n) is e = 1 - \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{n}, giving volumes

  V_S(T(2,3)) = \frac{\pi}{3}, \qquad
  V_S(T(2,5)) = \frac{3\pi}{5}, \qquad
  \frac{V_S(T(2,5))}{V_S(T(2,3))} = \frac{9}{5}.

The squaring exponent n_q = 2 reflects the meson's two-body composite structure: each quark constituent contributes one factor of the Seifert volume ratio to the geometric part of the mass formula. A power scan over exponents 1, 2, 3 is consistent with that reading, giving 290\;\mathrm{ppm} at n_q = 2 against 444{,}605\;\mathrm{ppm} at n_q = 1 and 799{,}479\;\mathrm{ppm} at n_q = 3. The scan is a weak check and is not offered as evidence for the exponent: the two-body rationale names n_q = 2 in advance, and the two alternatives miss by 44\% and 80\% rather than marginally, so a scan that selected the exponent against the data would look no different. What the scan establishes is only that the a-priori exponent is not contradicted.

Combining: (q_0^5 - q_0^{-5}) \times (9/5)^2 \approx 1.0914 \times 3.24 = 3.5361. \square

Computational witness

meson-kaon-pion-derivation.witness.json verifies the formula at 50-digit precision, confirms the algebraic identity q^5 - q^{-5} = h \cdot [5]_q, and validates the Seifert ratio V_S(T(2,5))/V_S(T(2,3)) = 9/5 exactly.

Lean structure — what is proved vs. the remaining gap

The Lean sibling separates the two algebraic identities (provable, sorry-free) from the physical / empirical content of the mass-ratio claim (not a Lean theorem). This makes precise what remains "to be proved" downstream.

Lean declaration content status
chi_21_odd \chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^n)=q^n+(-q^{-1})^n=q^n-q^{-n} for odd n proved (sorry-free)
seifert_ratio_T25_T23 V_S(T(2,5))/V_S(T(2,3))=9/5 proved (sorry-free; needs char \neq 2,3,5)
meson_squaring_exponent the exponent record n_q=2 proved (rfl)
mesonMassRatio the assembled formula \chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^5)\cdot(9/5)^2 definition

The gap (NOT Lean-proved, and intentionally so):

  1. The exponent n_q=2 has a physical rationale (two-quark composite) and is not contradicted by the power scan (290 ppm at n_q=2 vs 4.4\times 10^5 ppm at n_q=1). It is not derived from the substrate, and the scan does not supply the missing derivation — see the caveat in the proof body. The meson_squaring_exponent lemma only records the value; it does not select it.
  2. The canonical exact match to the PDG ratio (\approx 290 ppm) is a witnessed near-match, not a Lean equality — the witness JSON is the evidence, the Lean file proves only the two underlying identities.

Base-ring note. The Lean sibling is stated over a generic [Field R] (no archimedean $\mathbb{R}$ dependence). chi_21_odd is unconditional; seifert_ratio_T25_T23 carries explicit $2,3,5\neq 0$ hypotheses — the invertibility the rational identity genuinely needs, vacuous in any characteristic-0 specialisation. This avoids CharZero entirely and is verified sorry-free (lake env lean).

Scope — this is not the canonical route to m_K/m_\pi

This proof establishes the two algebraic identities above and assembles them into a witnessed near-match. It is not the framework's canonical closure of the meson ratio, and the two must not be conflated. The canonical route is the q-Clebsch--Gordan fusion together with the electromagnetic term, m_K^2/m_\pi^2 = [3]_q\,[4]_q + (\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}/\pi)\bigl(1 + \log(1+\hbar_q)\bigr) (prop:meson-em-sinh-closed-form), which is what the per-observable accuracy dashboard scores. The (q_0^5 - q_0^{-5})(9/5)^2 form here was formerly used there and was withdrawn from that role.

The two agree with each other only to about a part in 3\,400: the form proved here sits at 290 parts per million, which misses this observable's accuracy target of 263.6 parts per billion by a factor of 1{,}099, while the canonical route sits at 51.5 parts per billion. A reader who takes the 290 ppm figure as the framework's accuracy on m_K/m_\pi will be wrong by more than three orders of magnitude in the conservative direction.
